clue.text: A word from Mary, coming from the heart

definitions.text: A word from Mary, coming from the heart

parts.words: A word from Mary, coming from the heart
parts.note: surface reading: a heartfelt remark from someone called Mary
setter's reading: the place Mary Tudor said would be found engraved on her heart after she died

explanation.surface: A woman named Mary says something sincere and deeply felt.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen Mary I of England lost England's last French possession in 1558 and reportedly said that when she died the name of the town would be found lying in her heart.
explanation.definitionFit: The French port was the last English holding on the Continent, and its loss grieved the Tudor queen famously.

clue.text: First half of encyclopedia that's been split

wordplay.note: a multi-volume encyclopedia's first half runs from the letter A to the letter M

explanation.surface: Someone describes the opening volumes of a reference work that has been divided in two.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the first half as a volume label: A TO M.
explanation.definitionFit: Physicists famously split this smallest particle of an element, releasing nuclear energy.

clue.text: Has clues possibly about play's ending — as supplied by dramatist

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters sit around the next piece
possibly suggests the letters may form some other arrangement than the one given

parts.note: the anagram fodder, taken as written

indicators.note: a word's ending is its final letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the source word, a drama

explanation.surface: A crossword-like puzzle hints at how a play ends, supplied by its author.
explanation.definitionFit: Aeschylus was the earliest of the three great tragedians of ancient Athens, writer of the Oresteia.

clue.text: Agent going without sleep is irritable

indicators.note: going without is read as wearing on the outside, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: a secret agent
a short sleep

explanation.surface: A secret agent who has been deprived of rest becomes short-tempered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going without' looks like lacking, but here it means placed outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Snappy describes someone quick to speak sharply or crossly, the same as irritable.

clue.text: I really don't know what I expect a frisker to do

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a colloquial admission of ignorance

definitions.text: what I expect a frisker to do
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the instruction a person being frisked expects to be carried out on them

explanation.walkthrough: Someone frisking you searches your body, so the expected command is taken literally.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is a shrug said when asked something you cannot answer, and literally invites a body search.

clue.text: Suspension suspension?

parts.note: surface reading: a delay or temporary halt
setter's reading: a hanging, the kind of execution being put off

explanation.walkthrough: The first suspension is a postponement; the second is hanging from a rope, so the whole is a postponement of a hanging.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal reprieve delaying a death sentence is exactly a pause in carrying out a hanging.

clue.text: Aroma is spreading around middle of table — terrific food

indicators.note: around places the jumbled letters on either side of the next piece
something spreading loses its shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the anagram fodder, taken as written

indicators.note: middle of asks for the central letter of the five-letter word that follows

parts.note: the source word, a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: A lovely smell wafts across the dining table from a wonderful meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambrosia was the food of the Greek gods, hence any delicious dish; terrific is used in its sense of superb.

clue.text: American agency situated outside old city court in Rome

indicators.note: situated outside says the agency's letters stand on both sides of the next piece

parts.note: the Central Intelligence Agency
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A US intelligence agency is posted just beyond an ancient city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Curia is the papal administration and court that governs the Catholic Church from the Vatican.

clue.text: Old fellow with lots of bottle

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the biblical patriarch said to have lived 969 years
second meaning: a huge wine bottle holding eight standard bottles

explanation.walkthrough: Bottle is British slang for courage, so the surface suggests a very brave old man; here it is a literal wine container.
explanation.definitionFit: The Genesis patriarch is the byword for great age, and champagne makers named a giant bottle size after him.

clue.text: Creamy dish, mostly also known as "Greek food"

indicators.note: mostly means not all, so the dish loses its final letter

parts.note: a light whipped dessert
the standard abbreviation for also known as

explanation.surface: A menu note says a creamy dish mostly goes by another name, Greek food.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make Greek food look like the alias; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Moussaka is a baked Greek casserole of aubergine, minced lamb and white sauce.

clue.text: Reprimand despicable person in the course of social occasion

indicators.note: in the course of places one word during, and so inside, the other

parts.note: a bee is a gathering for work or fun, as in a sewing bee
a rat is a contemptible person

explanation.surface: Someone tells off a nasty guest at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: To berate is to scold someone angrily, a straightforward synonym for reprimand as a verb.

clue.text: This puma moves around river repeatedly — as may this creature

indicators.note: around puts the rearranged letters about the next pieces
when the letters move they take up a new order

parts.note: the anagram fodder, taken as written
the Po, Italy's longest river, taken twice

explanation.surface: A big cat paces back and forth along a river, as another animal might.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the animal, which does wander about in rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: The large African river horse spends its days wallowing in rivers and lakes, so it moves about in water.

clue.text: Duke heading off rebellion with transfer of authority

indicators.note: heading off means the word's first letter is removed

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for duke
an uprising against a government

explanation.surface: A nobleman forestalls an uprising by handing over some power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading off' looks like the duke preventing the revolt; it means beheading the rebellion word.
explanation.definitionFit: Devolution is the delegating of powers from central government to regional bodies, as with Scotland and Wales.

clue.text: It's by no means rare to get praise

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a steak cooked right through, the opposite of rare
second meaning: an exclamation congratulating someone

explanation.walkthrough: Rare looks like uncommon, but it is the steak-cooking term.
explanation.definitionFit: A steak cooked fully is the furthest from rare, and the same phrase is a common spoken compliment.

clue.text: Sinner always embracing form of idol

indicators.note: embracing means holding something inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: ever means always

indicators.note: a form of a word is that word reshaped, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A sinner keeps clinging to a carved idol, a picture of idolatry.
explanation.definitionFit: An evildoer is one who commits wicked acts, so a sinner in a looser, non-religious sense.

clue.text: A month with a big talker? One may go up the wall!

definitions.text: One may go up the wall!

parts.note: the standard short form of the last month of the year
a public speaker

explanation.surface: A month spent with a windbag would drive anyone up the wall.
explanation.walkthrough: To go up the wall is to become furious, but this one climbs a ladder to paint or paper it.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter and paperhanger literally climbs ladders against walls while working, a playful take on the idiom.

clue.text: Famous Roman watering hole coloured vermilion

parts.note: Cinna was a Roman politician, consul and conspirator against Caesar
a pub, slang watering hole

explanation.surface: A well-known Roman drinking spot is painted bright red.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinnabar is the red mercury ore from which vermilion pigment comes, and names that scarlet shade.

clue.text: What steeplejack must do as manoeuvre

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read in two parts: to con, study closely, the tall pointed top of a church
second meaning: to plot or scheme together

explanation.surface: A steeplejack has to move carefully about a church tower.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as CON SPIRE: to con is an old verb for to study or steer.
explanation.definitionFit: To conspire is to plot or scheme secretly, which manoeuvre as a verb also means.

clue.text: Noisy insect put off shy person

indicators.note: put off means sent away, so those letters are removed from the word

parts.note: clamant means loud and insistent
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A shy person is deterred by a loud buzzing bug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noisy insect' looks like one thing, a cicada perhaps; it is an adjective and a separate noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who clams up says nothing, so a clam is a reserved, uncommunicative individual.

clue.text: Rock agreeable to the audience

indicators.note: to the audience means as listeners would hear it spoken

parts.note: nice means pleasant or agreeable

explanation.surface: A rock performance goes down well with the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: Rock looks like music to suit the audience; it is the stone, whose G is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Gneiss is a banded metamorphic stone formed under heat and pressure.

clue.text: One sitting on the bench gets set alight by the match?

definitions.text: One sitting on the bench gets set alight by the match?

parts.words: One sitting on the bench gets set alight by the match?
parts.note: surface reading: a substitute on a sports team's bench gets fired up by the game
setter's reading: a gas burner standing on a laboratory bench, lit with a struck match

explanation.walkthrough: Bench and match point to football; the bench is a lab bench and the match a matchstick.
explanation.definitionFit: The gas burner named after chemist Robert Bunsen sits on lab benches and is lit with a match.

clue.text: Reduce rent

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to cut sharply, as with prices
second meaning: a tear or long cut in material

explanation.walkthrough: Rent looks like money paid to a landlord; it is a tear.
explanation.definitionFit: Shops cut prices drastically, and a gash in fabric is another name for a rip.

clue.text: See 13
Something sharp — one with cold's swallowed the medicine

indicators.note: swallowed means taken inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a barb is a sharp point
the Roman numeral for one
C for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A sharp-tongued patient with a cold has taken their dose of medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: The barb, placed first in the clue, is the outer piece that swallows the other two.
explanation.definitionFit: Bicarbonate of soda is a household antacid remedy, informally shortened to this.

clue.text: TV shows African dictator being given boot, terribly cross

indicators.note: terribly suggests the word is badly mangled, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: Idi Amin, the brutal ruler of Uganda in the 1970s
the anagram fodder, taken as written
a cross is the letter X

explanation.surface: A television programme shows a deposed African tyrant being kicked out, furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being given boot' reads as being sacked; boot is just fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a disparaging slang name for a television set, implying it dulls the mind.

clue.text: No hunter is out to become like the one being hunted

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or disordered, so these letters are put in a new order

parts.note: the anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who quits hunting ends up as the quarry instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A fugitive pursued by others is said to be fleeing and evading capture, the state of hunted prey.

clue.text: Writing doctrine as laid down by saint

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for saint
a set of beliefs

explanation.surface: A written statement of belief set out by a holy figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A screed is a long piece of writing, usually a tedious or ranting one.
